text:
support-jen: customer (AcmeCorp) opened a support escalation — p99s jumped from ~150ms to ~900ms on Dedicated us-west-2 around 2026-03-06 23:10 UTC. They see intermittent 500s and timeouts. Can ops triage? :warning:
kevin: seeing same alerts from our telemetry — Dedicated pool D-USW2-3 showing CPU wait and host IO stall spikes correlated with a driver roll on 2026-03-06 23:00 UTC. stack: higher queue depth and backend nvme latency.
raj: any deploys to infra around that time? I can check kube events and node oom/kick logs.
michelle: infra pushed a CUDA/driver bundle to D-USW2 nodes at ~22:55 UTC (driver build 531.79, nvme fw 2.3.1). We had a rolling that targeted dedicated capacity.
support-jen: customer repro steps: repeated a bunch of /v1/generate calls (concurrent 40 threads, prompt len ~512) and saw spikes after ~200s of load. sometimes requests 504, sometimes 500 with "backend read timeout".
kevin: here's a short log snippet from one affected node (kevin@d-usw2-3):
```
[mar06 23:12:05] svc: rq=120 queued=48 cpu_wait=0.62 io_wait=0.31
[mar06 23:12:06] nvme0n1: I/O 1234 timed out, qdepth 64 -> 2
[mar06 23:12:06] kworker/3: warning: nvme_io_completion delayed by 480ms
[mar06 23:12:07] model-runtime[pid=2145]: kvcache miss latency rising: p99=1.2s
```
raj: that nvme timeout line is bad. could be firmware interaction with the new driver scheduler. I'll start a host-level bisect: boot one node with previous driver build and run the same load.
michelle: good plan. also note Dedicated autoscaler attempted to place extra pods but they hit scheduling delays because of node-reported disk pressure briefly.
kevin: we reproduced on a spare node by applying the customer's exact load. with driver 531.79: p95 ~650ms, p99 ~1.1s, occasional 500s. with rollback to 529.12: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~260ms, no 500s.
support-jen: customer wants ETA and mitigation. can we route their traffic away from affected Dedicated pool or enable fallback?
michelle: immediate mitigations: (1) fail traffic for that customer to hosted API pool (temp) OR (2) route to a dedicated pool running the previous driver build (we have a small spare pool d-usw2-hot-legacy) and (3) throttle concurrent per-customer concurrency to 20 until we stabilize.
raj: I'm kicking off node-rollback on a canary subset (2 nodes) now. also opening a firmware/driver escalation with vendor — including nvme fw 2.3.1 logs.
sre-oncall: creating incident INC-2026-00123 and running playbook: preserve node logs, snapshot nvme smartctl, capture kernel oops, set observability retention for this incident.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-00123 created by sre-oncall at 2026-03-07T00:05:10Z. Pager triggered for infra-team.
kevin: repro commands I used for load (for debugging share only):
```bash
# stress test (concurrent clients 40, prompt len ~512)
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-8b", "input":"<long prompt>"}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
raj: notes from bisect so far — the NVMe completion latency climbs under sustained kernel IO with driver 531.79; previous driver doesn't show the same climb. suspect scheduling interaction between driver and kernel IO coop. I'll add perf counters and collect iostat -x 1 30 and blktrace during next run.
support-jen: customer update drafted: short explanation, mitigations in progress (failover to hosted pool and routing to legacy nodes), ETA 2 hours for initial mitigation.
michelle: operational tasks: (A) route acmecorp to d-usw2-hot-legacy (manual override in routing table), (B) throttle their concurrency, (C) add model fallback policy for their API key to a smaller model variant if latency persists. I'm applying A and B now.
kevin: A applied, B applied. their traffic shows rerouted and initial p95 dropped to ~200ms on hosted fallback. watching for errors.
raj: collecting deeper traces now — attaching next batch of dmesg + iostat. looking at nvme smart stats too.
sre-oncall: please add incident timeline notes: exact driver push time, node list affected, rollback windows, customer-visible mitigation times.
support-jen: customer acknowledged and accepted temporary hosted fallback. wants notes when fully resolved.
michelle: follow-ups: (1) vendor escalation: firmware/driver interaction investigation, (2) decide: full rollback vs vendor patch, (3) decide: add extra preflight for driver/firmware combos on Dedicated clusters.
kevin: I'll prepare a short postmortem stub once we have vendor response and final remediation.
raj: temp conclusion for now: regression strongly correlated with driver 531.79 rollout -> NVMe I/O queuing anomalies under sustained KV cache patterns. next: vendor triage, expand canary rollback if needed, keep customer on hosted fallback until resolved.
support-jen: thanks all — closing loop with customer after final remediation. :white_check_mark:
